why: The owner, 2026-11-04 12:20 AM MST: code that was written, much of it reverse-engineered over the past 2-3 weeks, was deleted from old trillion instead of being ported to its correct place, abandoned and covered up. Of the files old trillion lost from 2026-10-10 to 2026-11-04, 2,427 had no home in any new repository and no backlog row. So a commit or push that deletes a source or test file is refused unless each deleted file is named by a moved-from receipt in one of these checkouts, or by a retirement row that quotes a decision.

words.refused: {count} deleted source or test file(s) name no new home and no retirement decision. Move each with tools/move-code-between-trees (its moved-from.json receipt names the path), or retire it with a row in retired-paths.json whose decision quotes the person who decided ({ by, words, source }). 'Nothing imports it' and 'no row names it' are not decisions: they are a missing importer or a missing row.
words.one: {path}: no moved-from.json in {repositories} names it, and no retirement row with a decision covers it
